articles.title: Kaliningrad Under Attack For First Time as Plan to Pressure Exclave Escalates
articles.content:
Today a Russian vessel reportedly known for carrying military shipments has been struck in the Gulf of Finland by what is claimed to be Ukrainian drones:
Strikes were reportedly carried out against the Russian logistics vessel Sparta II, according to a report by Delfi, citing the Estonian Police and Border Guard Board.
During the attack, the cargo ship was located approximately 20 km off the coast of the Estonian island of Vaindloo in the Gulf of Finland.
The vessel Sparta II is known for its active transportation of weapons and cargo for the benefit of the Ministry of Defense. For example, it has repeatedly traveled between Russia and the port of Tartus in Syria, both before and after Assad’s departure.
The attack appeared to be carried out by aerial rather than naval drones:
The obvious question is where did they come from? Ukraine has no direct territorial line-of-sight to the Gulf of Finland, so obviously the drones either had to have been allowed to fly over NATO Baltic territory, or some Baltic region country would have had to assist Ukraine with naval assets from which to launch the drone or drones.
The vessel, as of the latest reports, is now fine and plans to continue on to its destination in Kaliningrad.
Shortly after, a reported Ukrainian attack on the Russian base of Baltiysk in Kaliningrad took place:
It was said to feature the first emergency sirens of the war in Kaliningrad:
Reports immediately claimed the drones were coming from Lithuania, at least according to the region’s Russian governor:
One channel attempted geolocations of the Russian tracer rounds seen in the videos:
They have geolocated the filming as from the D.a. Bro kitchen seen in the map below, with the yellow line representing the camera perspective looking southward. The radio tower visible in the video is circled in red:
I’ve used Grok bot to estimate the moon position for precisely that time of day, and it corresponds to a southerly position as seen in the video posted by the Coffe Report account. That means based on that geolocation, I would estimate the tracer rounds are firing in the southwesterly or westerly direction, as indicated by the light blue arrow above.
Coffe Report appears to have come to a similar conclusion:
Another video shows a circular stone structure near a railyard:
Which I’ve geolocated to 54.649893201029656, 19.905646131009448, seen here:
The direction the camera is looking is also southerly or toward the southeast (yellow arrow), and thus the tracer rounds likewise can be pinpointed to going in the westerly direction (green arrow):
Given that this base is at the very western outskirts of Kaliningrad, this appears to suggest the drones are coming out from the sea, and not from Lithuania:
However, it’s obviously possible other drones not seen in the videos did come from the Lithuanian direction—but we have no evidence of it yet apart from the Russian governor’s announcement.
The problem is, we all know Ukraine does not have an operable navy any longer, particularly not any ships that can reach the Baltic Sea from Ukraine. Thus, any drones launched from sea would have to utilize some form of “help” from NATO allies, whether using their containerized ships for transport or launched from allied territory to make it look like they are launched from sea for the purposes of plausible deniability.
We know Ukraine can launch aerial drones from naval drones, but there is no naval drone that can reach the Baltic Sea from Ukraine. One way or another, some NATO ally would have to have been an accomplice.
Pro-Ukrainian accounts have spread the theory that the drones traveled legally the long way through Russia:
What seems to make it plausible is the fact that Estonia did report drone alerts in two northeastern counties of the country corresponding to the orange encircled area above. This could have been more plausible if we hadn’t had months of direct confirmation that Ukrainian drones now regularly fly over allied NATO territory.
Also, if Ukrainian drones are capable of bypassing all of western Russia without being shot down, then why would they need to hook all the way around through the sea rather than also overflying Kaliningrad directly from the north-northeast to their target in Baltiysk? Why the need to hook all the way out to sea, then come from the west toward the east?
More and more, NATO has been goading Russia with talks of blockading Kaliningrad. The latest efforts are clearly part of a secret NATO-led strategy of “strategic ambiguity” and pressure against Kaliningrad in order to force Russia to escalate so that it can be labeled the aggressor.
According to Russian channel War Chronicle a variety of NATO assets were in the air near Kaliningrad:
NATO continues to direct Ukrainian forces towards the Leningrad region.
Governor Alexander Drozdenko reported that by 7 a.m. on November 21st, 49 drones had been shot down. In the days prior (November 19th and 20th), a Swedish reconnaissance aircraft, the Gulfstream S 102B Korpen, was operating in the direction of the Leningrad region, along with two NATO aircraft: NATO02 (LX-N90442), a flying radar E-3A Sentry, and RRR7220, a British Royal Air Force RC-135W Rivet Joint reconnaissance aircraft. Initially, the Swedish aircraft was the most active, and then the other two joined in gathering information.
It appears that the Ukrainian drones were once again flying over Estonian territory, as at 4:42 a.m. local time, the EE-ALARM alert system announced a possible drone threat in the Ida-Viru and Lääne-Viru counties. Residents of Väike-Maarja also reported “sounds similar to drones.”
Globalist luminary Anne Applebaum, married to Polish Deputy Prime Minister Radoslaw Sikorsky, seemed to spill the beans on what’s really happening behind the scenes in a recent interview with Tim Miller:
She states quite clearly that “behind the scenes” the European elites are quietly discussing how to escalate militarily against Russia, but that the public is not yet ready for this reality. After saying the quiet part out loud, she then appears to give the game plan away: Since a Europe-Russian war is “extremely unpopular” among the European masses, she laments that “unfortunately” only a “high casualty event”, like a Russian missile hitting a European city, can bring the hoi polloi around.
She disappointedly concludes that this hasn’t happened….yet.
Well, perhaps Russia has given them a first such warning, as Russian missiles allegedly landed in Poland yesterday only miles away from a NATO training ground:
One of the missiles that entered the airspace fell approximately 30 km from the Nowa Dęba training ground, where exercises Koalicja 26.2 are currently underway, involving countries from the “Coalition of the Willing” to deploy troops on Ukrainian territory after the end of the war.
The missiles and drones were simply flying without transponders. If they had been equipped with them, the Polish military would have immediately detected and prevented them, just as they do with saboteurs at the border.
Or at least that’s the official story—it could very well be another false flag with dummy missiles passed off as Russian. After all, they again blamed their favorite plausible deniability scapegoat of “bad weather” for their inability to intercept the missiles; this has been their go-to excuse for every previous psyop.
That’s not to mention the hilarity of the fact that Poland required the Germans’ permission to even shoot down a missile over their own Polish territory:
It’s clear that as Ukraine continues to sink further and further into unsustainable territory, Europe becomes ever more desperate to increase the pressure on Russia in any way possible. The goal is always the same: to force Russia to react aggressively in a way that can galvanize solidarity amongst the European masses whose job is to pay for the war on the Ukrainian side.
Unfortunately, Ukraine continues to slip into a budgetary abyss. Bulgaria recently announced they will not be joining the aid package to Ukraine, while Poland suspended funding for the NATO-led PURL initiative meant to buy weaponry for Ukraine.
All the while, Zelensky announced he needs $115B for next year, and no one knows where it will come from:

articles.title: Putin Calls Off Further Ceasefires as New Scale of European Involvement in Ukrainian War Uncovered
articles.content:
At the APEC summit in China earlier today, Putin made some very interesting remarks regarding the overall war in Ukraine and the strikes on the Crimean Bridge in particular.
When asked about the bridge attack, Putin stated that he personally gave the order long ago for the bridge to not be used for military purposes. As such, he claims that it was strictly a civilian object. It is true and interesting, that Western sources have published dozens of satellite photos over the past year or two showing alleged North Korean weapons shipments being sent to Russia, but they could not find a single photo of Russia delivering weapons supplies or military hardware over the Crimean Bridge.
But listen to the full answer:
Most significantly, Putin states that the attacks have now precluded any negotiations on mutual ceasefires. Many have interpreted this statement wrong, believing Putin has said there will no longer be any negotiations with Ukraine in general. That’s not what he said. He specifically explained that mutual ceasefires regarding the Black Sea or attacks on each other’s energy sectors will no longer be entertained—but this has nothing to do with the overall track of negotiations with the US toward a settlement of the conflict. Furthermore, he states that Russia’s response will be far more painful than the attack on the Crimean Bridge, and even as of this writing there are reports that a large fleet of Russian strategic bombers is preparing for the next wave of attacks against Ukraine.
The other interesting statement he made was in answer to the question of why Russia “takes it easy” on Ukraine. RT’s Editor-in-Chief Margarita Simonyan asked Putin whether it was Russia’s ingrained “nobility” of the soul which is responsible for the war being prosecuted in such a velvet glove way, noting that even Trump yesterday admitted that Russia is acting in a restrained manner against Ukraine and could be “far harsher” if it wanted to. Putin’s response was unexpected—it is not our nobleness, he states, but rather a diplomatic pragmatism which seeks to “leave room” for negotiations:
This answer will clearly come as a disappointment to most, and is somewhat baffling, to say the least. What diplomacy can there be with a government and system that Putin himself considers illegitimate, and to be a proxy controlled by hostile foreign powers? It seems likely that Putin’s less-than-candid response obscures some other more sensitive reality—but being present on a grand stage of diplomacy in China, Putin perhaps feels the need to portray a more diplomatic and amenable character.
Apparently, as part of the response Russia has already struck the Dutch embassy in Kiev, given that the Dutch company Destinus provided the Ruta missiles which took out the Crimean Bridge.
The Russian embassy in the Netherlands released this statement:
The full statement accuses Destinus employees of directly participating in the launching of missiles against Russia:
Statement by the Embassy of the Russian Federation in the Netherlands
On the Possible Involvement of Employees of a Dutch Defence Industry Company in Hostilities on the Side of the Ukrainian Armed Forces
❗️The Embassy has carefully examined reports in the Dutch media concerning the possible use of weapons against Russia by employees of Destinus in the Ukrainian conflict.
🔹The information published following a months-long journalistic investigation suggests that at least 40 employees of the company may have travelled to Ukraine at various times, where they allegedly took a direct part in combat launches of strike drones, including against targets on the territory of the Russian Federation.
🔹We note that numerous cases of civilian deaths and injuries, including those of children, resulting from terrorist drone attacks carried out by the Ukrainian Armed Forces have been recorded and documented. Responsibility for these attacks lies with all those involved in carrying out such launches in one way or another.
🔹In this regard, we find particularly noteworthy the assessments of Dutch experts in international humanitarian law interviewed by journalists, who draw a clear distinction between the supply of weapons and direct participation in hostilities, placing the activities of the company’s employees described in the reports in the latter category.
🔹Given the extensive government support provided to Destinus, including multimillion-euro contracts awarded by the Dutch Ministry of Defence, a number of legitimate questions arise regarding the extent to which the authorities of the Kingdom are aware of the nature of the company’s activities and exercise proper oversight thereof.
🔹We would specifically emphasise that, under international humanitarian law, civilians directly participating in hostilities lose their protection against attack and become legitimate targets.
🔹Against this backdrop, it is becoming increasingly difficult to regard the Netherlands as a mere bystander. Through its actions, The Hague is consistently deepening its involvement in the conflict, contributing to its prolongation and further escalation. As the Russian leadership has repeatedly emphasised, it is evident that every effort is being made in Europe to undermine a long-term peaceful settlement of the Ukrainian conflict. At the same time, it should be clearly understood that, regardless of any obstacles, our country will achieve all the stated objectives of the special military operation.
🔹The Embassy expects clear explanations from The Hague regarding the extent to which the Dutch authorities were aware of the possible involvement of employees of a national defence industry company in carrying out terrorist attacks against Russia.
The NL Times confirms:
Employees of the Dutch arms manufacturer Destinus have themselves participated in the war in Ukraine, NRC reported following a months-long investigation and interviews with over 40 people involved. They have hunted Russian drones in Ukraine and also assisted the Ukrainian military in launching attack drones toward Russia, dating back as far as 2023. The Dutch Ministry of Defense and experts in the field of armed conflict are concerned.
Read that again: “They have…assisted the Ukrainian military in launching attack drones toward Russia.”
Remember that for later.

articles.title: Bridge Wars: Ukraine and Russia Exchange Massive Blows as Crimean Bridge Goes Down
articles.content:
Earlier yesterday, Ukraine struck the famed Crimean Bridge with what was claimed to be a series of drones. Footage immediately spread, reportedly showing the bridge with severe damage to one of its arches, causing a “tilt”. A before (right) and after (left) comparison:
Hours later, at night Ukraine struck the bridge again, just as Russia unleashed a massive ballistic attack on Kiev which this time was said to have struck both the North and South bridges in the capital city.
The night time footage appeared to show the Crimean Bridge span deforming or collapsing after one of the hits—the second part shows exclusive footage of dozens of missiles striking the bridge while ineffective automatic fire fills the sky:
The fateful moment:
So, how did Ukraine manage to finally bring down the bridge? Did Russian air defenses “fail”?
Zelensky clued us in by providing an extensive list of weapons used, and it’s a long one:
For this, they used “Dovbush,” “Vendetta,” “Da Vinci,” “Sichen,” “Mich-2000,” “Ruta,” “Palianytsia,” “An-197,” “FP-1,” “FP-5 Flamingo,” and “R-360 Neptune.”
Today, at the key stage, the “Palianytsia” drones performed exceptionally well, striking the road section of the bridge, while “Neptune” missiles, “Ruta” drones, and FP-5 drones struck the railway section. Using “Flamingo,” our warriors carried out a precision-guided strike – and the communications uplink worked flawlessly until the very last seconds.
The official Ukrainian MOD account posted this video of assets used in the strikes:
In short, virtually every type of drone and missile in Ukraine’s arsenal was utilized to overwhelm the bridge, striking both the road ways, spans, arches, and everything in between.
In fact, even more secretive weapons were used that Zelensky appears to dare not name for political reasons. The Dutch defense firm Destinus posted the following message on their official LinkedIn site:
Note in particular that they claim their company’s Lord and Da Vinci drones were used to “suppress Russian air defenses” on the bridge. These drones are reported to be “multi-mission” and thus, in addition to their strike capability, have EW jamming abilities.
Russian Two Majors channel points out that Destinus is a partnership with German Rheinmetall:
Other sources identified a “rare” American RC-135 supporting the strikes from just outside Crimea as well:
From the above:
A USAF RC-135U Combat Sent, one of only two remaining in service, was tracked operating over the Black Sea after earlier missions near Kaliningrad and the Finnish-Russian border.
The aircraft flew from RAF Mildenhall and operated alongside other NATO assets, including an E-3A Sentry and supporting KC-135 tanker aircraft.
The mission comes amid heightened NATO surveillance activity around the Black Sea, where European and alliance aircraft have been particularly active in recent weeks.
The aircraft is designed to detect radar emissions, which makes its mission obvious:
RC-135 aircraft are designed to collect and analyse foreign radar emissions and other electronic signals. Among other things, this helps to gather intelligence on air defence systems.
Reportedly the craft passed near Crimea from ~12:10 to 16:30 UTC on November 16th. This puts its flight a few hours after the first strikes on the bridge (which happened in the early morning of November 16), and a few hours before the second strikes which collapsed the bridge (which happened very late evening November 16). One could almost theorize that the first strikes failed due to the effectiveness of Russian air defenses, and thus a second round of strikes was ordered this time with American help to identify and neutralize Russian AD systems.
Also, note the small ‘easter egg’ in Zelensky’s earlier official post. In the very end of the post, he notes:
Using “Flamingo,” our warriors carried out a precision-guided strike – and the communications uplink worked flawlessly until the very last seconds.
Here he is referencing the video he posted right after that quote, which apparently shows a camera onboard a Flamingo missile as it approaches the bridge:
The fact that he brags about this “flawless communications” uplink is interesting. He may be rubbing Russia’s face in the fact that Starlink terminals were used, or perhaps Western AWACS systems nearby feeding the missiles data back and forth. After all, the mapping of the missile route was as follows:
This puts the orientation of the route somewhere like this:
This is precisely why an AWACS system would have been necessary to stop such attacks. It would be able to scan and identify such threats over the Black Sea from a far greater distance, though reportedly Russia may be using other fighter jets like Mig-31s and Su-30SMs in an AWACS role around the Black Sea area, but these have far lower flight ranges and cannot stay up in the sky nearly as long.
FighterBomber chimes in:
He makes one error about the trajectory of the attack: It was definitely geolocated from the south (Black Sea direction), not the “rear” (Azov Sea direction) of the bridge as he supposes.
But that is only for the footage seen from the Flamingo—other assets could have came from the north.
What we can conclude is that this was a very large, complex, multi-nation operation which required the cooperation of the entire Western-NATO alliance to succeed. It was done for two reasons. The short term one: Zelensky needed to embarrass Putin for the upcoming trilateral US-Russia-China meeting at the Shenzhen APEC summit. This will be an unprecedented Potsdam Conference-like face-to-face between Xi, Trump, and Putin. Feeling sidelined and losing control to the wills of the greater powers, Zelensky needed to “remind” his sponsors that he still has “cards” to play.
The Times agrees:
The more macro and longer-term reason is a familiar one. Everytime Ukraine begins to face dire straits, it needs a huge new PR hit to stave off collapse. Zelensky’s various big PR initiatives of the past six months have all either failed or now been halted. For instance, the AFU’s various shortlived advances along the front have mostly abated, with Russian forces now resuming advances in many areas, particularly the Dobropillya and Zaporozhye regions. The various refinery strike and “closing of the skies” campaigns have all failed to produce any appreciable results. Likewise, the “Crimean isolation” operation failed after Ukrainian strikes along the various routes were slowly stifled, perhaps partly by Starshield slowdowns and partly by Russian defensive innovations and road network redundancies.
Now, facing his most crippling winter ever, and a new Russian strike campaign that is shutting down major Ukrainian cities, not to mention dwindling Western military aid, Zelensky needed a new big headline PR moment to grab attention and present Ukraine as still “in the game”. But while the Crimean Bridge was a shiny holy grail object for Zelensky, it does not represent a strategically important objective, given that Russia has already constructed many redundancies. It will only affect civilians in Crimea with an inconvenience of having to use ferries or travel the longer north route to get back to mainland Russia.

articles.title: Spate of Odd Cyber-Outages Strikes US as Nations Worldwide Warn of “Mystery” Threat
articles.content:
Something eerie is afoot.
For the past few weeks, Western countries have begun playing up some unknown disaster or “event”, with UK in particular issuing breathless warnings to its citizens to stockpile goods and make emergency plans in case of some mysterious “disruptions”:
The BBC called it the coming “Black Sky” event:
"We are nine meals from anarchy" is a phrase often heard in the civil contingency world. A brutal reminder of the fear that three days without food would be enough to turn a crisis into chaos. If a Black Sky event takes out electricity, water, shops and communications, there is a good reason the government wants us to have our own supplies.
The BBC author plays up the threat by claiming he already experienced a dark “omen” even whilst writing the above article:
While writing this piece last Saturday I had to break off for an hour because my street was suddenly plunged into darkness. We had a power cut.
I found my emergency torch, but the batteries had leaked. My candles had been pushed to the back of a cupboard and I had no idea where I had put my wind-up radio with its emergency torch.
It felt like an omen.
One would assume such warnings are related to psyops about some Russian attack, but this seems different. Reading between the lines, we infer that TPTB are pushing some kind of nationwide power outage perhaps by way of “cyber attack” whom they can blame on a convenient actor for the purpose of pushing through a much darker and broader agenda.
This campaign has likewise accelerated in the US, where the FBI has warned of some unknown attacks against municipal water systems.
In the meantime, major and historic disruptions have occurred over the past few months. These include the Hugging Face incident, where OpenAI agents broke out of their containment and spread through the internet, followed by the recent widespread Microsoft outages.
Two days ago—on the ominous date of Friday the 13th—the US suddenly experienced an unprecedented nationwide disruption to the FAA flight systems, which caused the issuance of a ground stop to all flights in the country.
After some mealymouthed responses regarding the nature of the disruptions, US authorities finally claimed the issue was caused by “old equipment” at FAA sites:
Just watch the video above. Following the saga, the weirdly equivocating responses from authorities were not very reassuring, or believable for that matter. It made it easy to conclude that something is being hidden—though perhaps it is only embarrassment.
Many suspected a coverup for an Iranian attack, while conspiracy theorists naturally assumed this was either a practice run to some major cyber false flag, or perhaps the consequences of an ongoing AI containment incident. Many now believe in the wake of the Hugging Face incident, some super intelligent AIs have escaped, cloned themselves on the internet, and are proceeding to compromise and disrupt various security systems worldwide.
The Secretary of the DHS even seemed to indirectly admit that this was a possibility:
Granted, we must not forget the eternal Hanlon’s Law: “Never attribute to malice that which is adequately explained by stupidity.”
And there is plenty of that—or at least incompetence and obsolescence—when it comes to the US power grid and general infrastructure. Shockingly, it was revealed that the FAA still runs floppy disks on much of its critical “computer” system networks:
WASHINGTON, Nov 5 (Reuters) - The US Federal Aviation Administration said on Thursday it will replace by the end of 2028 the outdated floppy disks used for weather and other critical information at more than 400 air traffic control facilities across the country.
The Enterprise Information Display System will replace four systems dating back to the 1980s and will put important operational information in one place so controllers can quickly see air traffic updates.
It’s certainly believable that simple incompetence can be at fault. But the preponderance of related odd events in sequence over the past few months is rather suspicious.
If that weren’t enough, the Pentagon launched what was being billed as a “doomsday plan” called Fortress America, an initiative for making US military bases self-sufficient in the event of some mass power grid failure:
Why the need for all these preparations all of the sudden?
Now the Mossad has reportedly warned the US that Iran is planning some major “attack” on American leaders, allegedly causing some officials to be transferred to secure facilities:
Barak Ravid of Axios—who knows a thing or two about the Mossad—not surprisingly reveals that the Mossad chief is currently in Washington to help deliver Netanyahu’s urgent pleas to resume the war with Iran:
Why it matters: The visit by Roman Gofman, one of Benjamin Netanyahu’s closest confidants, comes as the Israeli prime minister is pressing President Trump to resume the war against Iran.
Driving the news: Gofman is meeting with CIA Director John Ratcliffe, the sources said. He is also expected to travel to Miami to meet White House envoy Steve Witkoff, one of the sources said.
Surprise, surprise. Can we all see how the threads are tying together?
It’s not a far stretch to hypothesize that some of the recent psyops, false flags, and played up “threats” may be designed to further goad the US into finishing off Iran. But given the similar warnings in Europe, there is a feeling that something bigger is at play.
We know that for a long time the WEF-aligned elites had planned for another COVID-style lockdown, this time from an unnamed “cyber” threat:
It’s hard to parse between the various interwoven threads, but it’s clear there are major incentives for the elites to push these new cyber threats for a variety of related purposes. A populace in fear is one easy to browbeat into accepting hard-to-swallow consequences. On the lower end of the scale, it’s obvious that Israel may seek to stage a false flag to blame on Iran to tip Trump into finishing off its arch nemesis. On the higher end of the scale, the elites appear to be preparing to use the opportunity created by AI cyber threats to continue pushing their 2030 agenda of global centralization. Somewhere in that muddle is the genuine case of US infrastructure creaking along, one last straw away from imploding.
So, what do you make of it?
